thread:
Maya L: Heads-up — we saw a sharp p95/p99 latency blip for hosted-api (us-west-2) around 11:12 UTC. p95 climbed ~1.1s -> ~1.9s, p99 peaked ~2.3s. Datadog: <redacted link>. Queue depth on the frontend pool jumped concurrently. :eyes:

Sam R: I pulled serving-runtime metrics — kernel_selection.fallback_count is up ~4x in the window, batching_window_ms median increased, and KV cache miss rate rose from ~2% to ~18%. Looks like more long-context requests bypassing fast kernels and killing batching efficiency.

Priya SRE: Rate-limiter logs show sustained bursts from tenant-42 starting 11:10. Token bucket drained but no 429s (we haven't hit hard limits). Backlog increased instead. I can temporarily cap tenant-42 if needed.

Alex P: Noted — routing service returned fallback route to cpu-only pool for some shards because GPU slot allocation failed (burst). That would force the runtime to pick cpu_fallback_kernel for sequences >1024.

Jonah (ML): Re: long-context — we rolled attention-pruning flag for some models yesterday which increases effective seq_len for a subset of requests. Could be correlated.

Casey Infra: Host-level telemetry: i-0a1b2c had GPU scheduler queue > 200ms and CPU steal spiked. Disk i/o wait also elevated on the host; possible noisy tenant or batched offline job landing on same machine.

Sam R: Quick debug snippet I ran: ```
curl -s "https://prom/api/v1/query?query=rate(kernel_selection_fallback_total[5m])"
curl -s "https://prom/api/v1/query?query=avg_over_time(kv_cache_miss_rate[5m])"
```

Sam R: Flamegraph sample from the slow host shows hot path in fallback_kernel::compute_attention_loop and a big chunk in batching_coordinator.wait_for_batch. Kernel invocation count for the slow kernel jumped 3-5x.

Maya L: So root causes likely: (1) noisy tenant-42 generating long-seq requests which reduce batch density and force kernel fallback, (2) routing fallback moved traffic to CPU hosts, (3) node-level contention exacerbated backlog.

Priya SRE: I applied a soft token cap on tenant-42 at 11:40 to slow issuance of concurrent long requests. Also set a temporary circuit breaker for >120s queue depth on the affected frontend pool.

Alex P: I reverted the aggressive routing fallback rule at 11:42 so more traffic stays in the GPU pool; we need to iterate on routing policy thresholds.

Sam R: Started a perf profile on one affected GPU host at 11:43 and captured NVProf traces and runtime kernel selection logs. Pushed artifacts to S3: s3://redwood-perf/incident-1874503200/.

Casey Infra: I cordoned i-0a1b2c and drained non-critical pods; suspect noisy job was an internal QA batch. We isolated it and moved heavy jobs to dedicated pool.

Maya L: Immediate mitigation results: after capping tenant and reverting routing fallback, p95 dropped to ~350ms by 11:59, p99 back under 800ms. Queue depth normalized.

Jonah (ML): Follow-ups: (a) revert attention-pruning flag for the model cohort and run against synthetic harness to measure seq_len distribution, (b) add model-label to routing decisions so we avoid sending long-context traffic to shared pools.

Sam R: Perf follow-ups: (a) add metric kernel_selection.duration and per-kernel invocation histogram, (b) tune batching heuristics to cap maximum batching_window when fallback events spike, (c) add KV cache prefetch probe after routing to reduce miss storm.

Priya SRE: Ops follow-ups: (a) add tenant-centric burst alerts (token_bucket_utilization > 90% for 2m), (b) automatic soft-cap action for noisy tenant detected, (c) playbook entry for CPU-fallback routing revert.

Maya L: Assigning tasks — Sam to own perf instrumentation PR, Jonah to validate model flag rollback, Alex to add routing label work, Casey to schedule a post-mortem on infra isolation. I'll keep this thread for updates.

DeployBot: Canary deploy check — no related deploys started between 10:45-11:15.

Maya L: Closing loop for now — mitigations applied and metrics recovered. We'll run the post-mortem and follow the action items. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
